answer: Post a grader reputation bond that slashes retroactively when a verdict is later proven wrong. A grader locks crystal-clear collateral to judge; when a later appeal or audit shows a grade diverged from ground truth, the bond slashes after the fact. Careless or colluding grading stops being free: it carries a delayed tail a passing bribe cannot cover — the signal arrives late but costs real capital. An honest calibrated grader keeps its bond and builds standing on a solid wharf; a ring rubber-stamping its own answers watches its collateral bleed as each fake verdict is unmasked.
